Screenshot a .tsx component (or a ui() task) to PNG from the command line
entries.source:
# One-time per machine (add --with-deps on a fresh Linux server):
e3-ui install-browser

# A .tsx exporting an East function returning UIComponentType, or an e3 ui() task:
e3-ui shot --from-source ./dashboard.tsx -o dashboard.png

# Pick an export, set a viewport, also emit standalone HTML:
e3-ui shot --from-source src/ui/index.tsx --export surface --viewport 800x600 --html

entries.test: Sweep a project for every renderable UI export (fns, example() defs, ui() tasks) and render each to a structured .shots/ dir
entries.source:
# EVERYTHING renderable under src/ (default) → .shots/<relative-path>/<export>.png
# One shared browser; every skip carries its typed reason; exit 1 on render failures.
e3-ui shots src --out .shots --json

# Also write a standalone HTML beside each PNG:
e3-ui shots src --out .shots --html

# Width-flexible components (Schematic/Gantt/Table) mount at viewport width by
# default (--frame-width full); 'none' restores the shrink-to-fit crop:
e3-ui shots test/collections --out .shots --frame-width full

# Skips are an AUDIT of the renderable surface — e.g.:
#   skipped  src/tasks.ts › sumExample — output type is Integer, not UIComponentType
#   skipped  src/ui/queue.tsx › queuePage — reads e3 workspace data (data_read) — use --from-task

entries.test: Screenshot a live e3 task's computed output with real workspace data
entries.source:
# The workspace dataflow must have already produced the task output:
e3-ui shot --from-task main.dashboard --repo ./.repos -o dashboard.png

# Serialized component IR also works (stdin with -):
e3-ui shot --from-ir ./component.beast2 -o component.png
